title: Cream cheese frosting
summary: Tangy, spreadable cream cheese frosting sweetened with powdered erythritol, for carrot cake, spice cakes and cupcakes.
steps: Beat the butter on medium speed until creamy, about 1 minute.
Add the cream cheese and beat just until smooth and combined. Over-beating cream cheese makes the frosting runny.
Add the powdered erythritol, vanilla and salt and beat on low until incorporated, then on medium for 30 seconds.
If it is too stiff to spread, beat in the cream a teaspoon at a time.
Frost a cooled cake. Keep frosted cakes refrigerated.
dairy_free_notes: Dairy-free cream cheese gives a softer, less tangy frosting; chill it 20–30 minutes before spreading and add a squeeze of lemon juice for tang.
tips: Both cream cheese and butter should be soft but still cool; warm ingredients make a loose frosting.
Erythritol can taste slightly cooling here; replacing a quarter of it with allulose softens that.

origin.history: Cream cheese was first sold commercially in New York State in the 1870s. Frostings made by beating it with butter and sugar became an American staple in the mid-1900s, closely tied to carrot cake and, later, red velvet cake. It remains the classic topping for both.
